summary: Controlled workshop study holding the model fixed and varying the harness: Qwen 3.6 Plus and MiniMax M2.5 run through Goose, OpenCode and OpenHands-SDK (via Harbor, Daytona sandboxes, 900 s cap) on a stratified 50-task subset of Terminal-Bench Pro, one trial per cell (300 trials). Pass rates differ by only 0–8 pp within a model (CIs mostly include zero), while reported tokens per solved task differ up to ~40x and failure-mode profiles replicate across models.

claims.claim: Harness choice induces up to 40x difference in tokens per solved task
claims.evidence: Table 3: Goose 28,142 / 36,950 vs OpenCode 1,147,740 / 1,546,977 tokens per solve; bootstrap CIs non-overlapping (§4.2). But token accounting differs by harness: OpenCode/OpenHands totals include cached tokens via ATIF, Goose uses a total-only field (§3.5, §6), and §4.2 itself lists 'harness-specific token accounting' as a possible cause, so part of the gap may be measurement, not cost.

claims.claim: Within-model pass-rate differences across harnesses are small (0–8 pp)
claims.evidence: Table 2 with 95% paired bootstrap CIs; largest gap Goose vs OpenCode on MiniMax −8.0 pp [−18.0, 0.0]. n=50, single trial per task.

claims.claim: Failure fingerprints are harness properties that replicate across models
claims.evidence: Table 4: Goose REASON-dominated (20/15) with zero VERIFY; OpenHands-SDK VERIFY 6/8 and MAX_TURNS 6/6; OpenCode TIME/HANG with no MAX_TURNS (because it has no turn cap). Two models only; post-hoc rule-based classifier (App. A) not validated against human labels; the OpenCode fingerprint is partly an artefact of budget asymmetry.

claims.claim: No-action turns explain the cost gap (10x more for OpenCode)
claims.evidence: Fig. 2: 2.0–2.16 vs 0.2–0.3 no-action turns per task; mechanistic link is argued ('consistent with'), not tested.

patterns.note: Shows model-name leaderboards conflate harness effects; recommends reporting harness specs, tokens, latency and failure vectors.
Recommends choosing harness–model pairs by pass rate under token/latency budgets; budget controls (turn caps) materially change failure profiles.
Per-trial logs, failure categories and no-action-turn metrics used as observability signals; raw logs released.
Daytona sandbox per task held constant.
Same four-skill operational playbook injected into all harnesses; not varied.

methodology.sample: 50 of 200 Terminal-Bench Pro tasks, stratified over 8 GPT-4o-mini-assigned categories; 3 harnesses x 2 models x 1 trial = 300 trials
methodology.baselines: Harnesses compared against each other; no single 'proposed' system
methodology.models: Qwen 3.6 Plus, MiniMax M2.5 via OpenRouter default sampling
methodology.variance: 95% paired-task bootstrap CIs (B=10,000) on pass rate and tokens/solve; single trial per task-cell, so run-to-run variance is not measured

standards.peer_review: Under review at DL4C Workshop @ ICML 2026; preliminary, 7 pages
standards.artifacts: Anonymized configs, raw trial logs, aggregated snapshots and analysis scripts (anonymous.4open.science); 50 task IDs in Appendix B
standards.preregistration: Task set fixed before runs and no tasks removed (§3.5); not formally preregistered

biases.detail: n=50 tasks, one trial each; one task = 2 pp.
Token totals are not measured identically across harnesses (cached tokens included for two, total-only for Goose), weakening the 40x cost interpretation.
OpenCode has no turn cap (wall-time only) while others cap at 40 turns, which shapes the failure fingerprints being compared.
Bootstrap is over tasks; no repeated runs, with provider-default sampling that may change between runs (§6).

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Goose, OpenCode, OpenHands-SDK (none by the authors); Alibaba and MiniMax models
coi.detail: Authors do not ship any evaluated harness or model as far as the text shows.

verdict_reason: Well-controlled, honestly hedged harness-vs-model study with CIs and released logs, but small n, single trials, two models, and non-uniform token accounting that may inflate the headline 40x figure.
applicability: Directly relevant to a team running mixed agent hosts: pass rate barely moves across harnesses, but cost, latency and failure style (stop-when-stuck vs persist-to-plausible vs spin-until-timeout) differ by harness. The team should treat host+model pairs as the evaluation unit, measure tokens per accepted change and failure categories per host on its own Java services tasks, and set explicit turn/time budgets uniformly across hosts. A host whose failures skew to 'plausible but wrong' (VERIFY) needs stronger spec-driven acceptance tests and review gates. The Terminal-Bench tasks are not Java multi-repo work, so absolute numbers do not transfer.

conflicts_with.detail: NOOA reports consistent single-run pass-rate wins of a few points over OpenCode and PI; this study shows gaps of that size between open harnesses are mostly within bootstrap noise at n=50.
